1.s: Paul writes from prison to his friend Philemon about Onesimus, a runaway slave who became a Christian with Paul. He asks Philemon to receive him “no longer as a slave, but more than a slave, a beloved brother,” and offers to pay any debt himself.
1.d: Onesimus means “useful”, so “once was useless to you, but now is useful” is probably a play on his name [[tosn:Philemon 1:11]] [[bible:Philemon 1:11]]. The letter is also addressed to the church that met in Philemon’s home [[tosn:Philemon 1:2]]. Paul asks him to receive Onesimus “no longer as a slave, but more than a slave, a beloved brother” [[bible:Philemon 1:16]].
